title: Parrot Catapult: Avocado Trajectory Lab
description: A physics sandbox where the user loads avocados onto a catapult operated by an animated parrot. The user adjusts launch angle, spring tension, wind resistance, and spin rate, then launches avocados at floating ring targets. Real-time trajectory arcs, bounce physics on platforms, and scoring based on accuracy are displayed.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load shared_assets/Parrot.glb as an animated parrot perched on a wooden catapult arm (build the catapult from BoxGeometry and CylinderGeometry primitives, brown MeshStandardMaterial). Load shared_assets/Avocado.glb as the projectile, scaled to roughly 0.3 units, placed in the catapult bucket. Scene setup: ground plane with grid texture, soft blue sky background color, DirectionalLight with shadows enabled, AmbientLight for fill. Place 5 floating ring targets (TorusGeometry, golden emissive material) at varying distances (10-40 units) and heights (3-12 units) in front of the catapult. Camera starts at a 3/4 view using OrbitControls. Build an HTML/CSS overlay control panel with these interactive parameters: (1) Launch Angle slider 15-75 degrees, default 45, (2) Spring Tension slider 5-25 N, default 15, (3) Wind Speed slider -5 to 5 m/s horizontal, default 0, (4) Avocado Spin Rate slider 0-10 rad/s, default 2, (5) Gravity multiplier slider 0.5-2.0, default 1.0. Add a Launch button. When clicked, animate the parrot playing its wing-flap animation (use AnimationMixer), tilt the catapult arm upward to the set angle over 0.3 seconds, then release the avocado along a parabolic trajectory computed each frame using projectile motion equations: x += vx*dt + 0.5*wind*dt^2, y += vy*dt - 0.5*g*gravity_mult*dt^2, and rotate the avocado mesh by spin_rate*dt around its forward axis. Draw a fading trail line (BufferGeometry updated each frame, LineBasicMaterial with opacity). Detect collision with ring targets using distance checks (within 0.8 units of torus center counts as a pass-through). On hit, flash the ring green and increment a score counter displayed on screen. On ground collision (y<=0.15), simulate a single bounce at 40% energy restitution then stop. Add a Reset button that returns the avocado to the catapult. Display real-time stats: current velocity magnitude, max height reached, and total distance traveled. Validate all slider values are within their defined ranges before allowing launch.
